title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Ops & Top Issues
author: Alex Chen
summary: This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues + canonical fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, high-quality docs that reduce onboarding time, lower support load, and streamline updates for SDKs and API examples.
scope: Applies to all DevEx-authored content under confluence/eng-developer-experience (SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and docs-site operations). Excludes product PRDs and platform runbooks owned by other teams.
ownership_and_maintenance: Primary owner: Developer Experience team (eng-developer-experience). Doc steward: Alex Chen. Review cadence: quarterly reviews for SDK guides and API examples; monthly review for top support issues. Major updates (breaking API/SDK changes) must include a migration guide and be reviewed by Product and Applied ML teams.
naming_and_location_conventions:
- File names: short descriptive hyphenated words with date suffix when needed (e.g., developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-api-examples-2026-04-20.json).
- Location: Store canonical versions under confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates or /docs-site for operating procedures.
- Title field: sentence case, descriptive.
- Labels: include at least one of: sdk, quickstart, api-example, playbook, ops.
- Related_pages: link to design docs, ADRs, and release notes when applicable.
templates_and_content_structure:
All DevEx pages should follow this standard structure:

1) Title and 1-line summary
2) Short intro (3-5 sentences)
3) When to use this doc (audience and prerequisites)
4) Step-by-step quickstarts or examples (numbered)
5) Reference: API/CLI/SDK snippets and configuration table(s)
6) Troubleshooting / top support issues
7) Ownership, review cadence, and related pages

Use headings, short paragraphs, bullets, numbered procedures, and small code blocks (<= 40 lines). Keep examples runnable and copy-paste friendly. Avoid large exploratory content or meeting notes.
sdk_guides:
Purpose: Provide language-specific SDK usage patterns, auth, error handling, and best practices.

Required sections per SDK guide:
- Quickstart (hello world): minimal auth + request example for text generation and embeddings.
- Installation: package manager commands and supported versions.
- Authentication: env var names, token scopes, and refresh guidelines.
- Common patterns: streaming, function/tool calling, batching, and retry/backoff examples.
- Error handling: mapping of HTTP codes to recommended client behavior (e.g., 429 -> exponential backoff with jitter; 503 -> retry with longer backoff or fallback to lower-cost model).
- Migration notes: when behavior changes across SDK versions.

Example snippet (JavaScript):
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generateText({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', prompt: 'Summarize the following...' });
console.log(resp.text);

Publish checklist before marking SDK guide as published:
- Lint (docs linting) passes
- Snippets execute in CI smoke tests (see docs-ci job)
- Reviewed by at least one SDK engineer and one product engineer
- Versioned and linked from API reference
quickstarts_and_templates:
Goal: Provide opinionated, minimal examples that get developers to a working call in under 5 minutes. Quickstarts should be 10-25 lines of code and include: prerequisites, environment setup, step-by-step commands, and a one-minute test.

Standard quickstart template (copyable):
- Title: One-line descriptor (e.g., 'Node.js: text generation quickstart')
- Audience & prerequisites (node >=16, API key)
- Install command (npm/yarn/pip)
- Minimal example (auth + request + print)
- Expected output and troubleshooting section (common failure patterns)

Example Node quickstart:
1) npm install @redwood/inference-js
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx
3) node quickstart.js (quickstart.js contains the snippet above)

Template for internal templates folder: include a README.md describing variants (streaming, tool-calling, long-context), a small test harness (python/ts) in /examples, and an OWNERS file listing reviewers.
api_examples_and_conventions:
API examples must be authoritative and reflect the current public API surface. Conventions:
- Provide examples for REST + official SDKs (JS, Python, Go).
- Use realistic prompts and explain parameter trade-offs (temperature, top_p, max_tokens).
- Show streaming and non-streaming variants.
- Include function/tool calling example and structured output parsing example.

Example REST curl (text generation):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"Explain the benefits of caching for LLM inference.","max_tokens":150}'

Keep examples small, comment key parameters, and ensure the example responses are plausible but truncated. All REST examples must include an SDK equivalent.
docs_site_operating_procedures:
Purpose: Keep the docs site reliable, reproducible, and easy to update.

Key items:
- Docs CI: repo 'devex/docs' runs on PRs. Jobs: lint, snippet-smoke-test (runs examples in isolated env), build (mkdocs), and deploy (to docs.redwood.ai staging).
- Release flow for docs:
  1) Create feature branch and update JSON doc(s).
  2) Open PR with link to related changelog/PR that necessitates doc change.
  3) CI must pass (including snippet smoke tests).
  4) At least one reviewer from DevEx and one from Product must approve.
  5) Merge to main will deploy to staging; tag release (docs/vYYYY-MM-DD) to promote to production.
- Emergency docs patch: open PR with 'emergency/docs' label, ping #devex on Slack, and a senior engineer will fast-track review within 2 business hours.
- Docs availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for production site. On-call: Engineering SRE team owns uptime; DevEx handles content rollbacks and hotfixes.
pr_and_release_checklist:
Before merging any published doc update: 
- All code snippets included in the doc must be covered by snippet-smoke-test.
- Update 'last_updated' field in JSON.
- Add or update related_pages and labels.
- Confirm OWNERS file includes at least one approver.
- For breaking changes, include a migration guide and cross-link to release notes.
- Run 'make docs-build' locally and sanity-check the new page.
Commands: 
- make docs-build && ./scripts/deploy-docs.sh --staging
- ./scripts/run-snippets.sh --ci
- git tag -a docs/v2026-04-20 -m 'Docs: update SDK quickstarts'
top_support_issues_and_canonical_fixes:
This section lists the highest-frequency support issues seen in the last 12 months, with concise, canonical fixes to reduce ticket churn. Review monthly and add new items to the top-support list.

1) Issue: Developers get 401/403 when using new API keys after rotation.
   Canonical fix: Confirm env var REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in the process where the call is made (CI/CD, serverless env). If rotating keys, perform the following: 
     a) create new key in Console -> API Keys,
     b) update CI secret store,
     c) deploy,
     d) revoke old key once traffic is verified.
   Notes: add sample CI config for GitHub Actions secrets and Vault (see example snippet).

2) Issue: Streaming responses appear truncated for long responses.
   Canonical fix: Ensure client uses streaming cursor and drains the stream until EOF. In JS SDK, use `client.stream()` and await `for await (const chunk of stream) {}`. For serverless environments, increase function timeout to 60s or longer depending on expected token volume.

3) Issue: 429 rate-limits during bursts.
   Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter, and enable client-side batching where possible. Recommended policy: initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=10s, attempts=6. If customer sees regular 429s, recommend upgrading to Dedicated or configuring smart-routing to a lower-utilization region.

4) Issue: SDK snippet in docs no longer runs in CI after dependency bump.
   Canonical fix: Pin snippet run images to major/minor SDK versions in docs CI, and add a nightly job that runs examples against the latest SDK to detect regressions early.

5) Issue: Confusing parameter names between REST and SDK (e.g., max_tokens vs token_limit).
   Canonical fix: Maintain a 'param map' table within the SDK guide and always show both REST and SDK equivalents on the same page.

Each canonical fix must include: scope, root cause, step-by-step reproduction, and a minimal remediation example. Store these in a machine-readable table in the docs repo for use in support automation.
troubleshooting_and_escalation:
If a doc-related issue requires a code or infra change (e.g., broken snippet image in CI):
1) Triage in #devex-support with severity label (low/medium/high/critical).
2) For critical (docs site down, broken auth examples leaking secrets): page owner and on-call SRE must be paged.
3) Follow incident runbook for rolling back to last known-good tag (git tag docs/vYYYY-MM-DD).

Contact matrix: DevEx owner (Alex Chen) -> DevEx lead (Priya Singh) -> Eng SRE on-call.
metrics_and_impact:
Track the following metrics monthly: 
- Page views and time-to-first-byte for docs site pages (by page)
- Number of support tickets referencing docs (goal: decrease 20% YoY)
- Snippet CI pass rate (target: 100% on main)
- Mean time to publish approved doc (goal: <= 3 business days)

Use these metrics to prioritize which quickstarts and canonical fixes to expand into full troubleshooting guides.
